title: Timing Side-Channels in Anonymous AE
summary: Anonymous AE's timing side-channel can reveal whether a nonce was anticipated; modeling, analyzing, and eliminating it remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For Anonymous AE, the unresolved research task is to model, analyze, and eliminate timing side-channels arising from the use of $L_x$ and $N_x$. Phase 1 processes only headers in $L_x$ and is expected to be faster than Phase 2; this timing difference can leak information about whether a nonce was anticipated. A complete resolution must therefore characterize the timing leakage associated with these two phases and provide a way to eliminate it while preserving the stated operation of Anonymous AE.

scope.domain: Timing side-channel analysis of the Anonymous AE authenticated-encryption construction.
parameters: Lx and Nx: named objects whose use gives rise to the timing side-channel
Phase 1 and Phase 2: processing phases whose relative timing is at issue
scope.unresolved_remainder: Model, analyze, and eliminate the timing side-channels arising from use of Lx and Nx, including the leakage caused by the timing difference between Phase 1 and Phase 2, while preserving Anonymous AE's stated operation.

progress.summary: The source explicitly labels the modeling, analysis, and elimination of timing side-channels as an open problem. It links the issue to Phase 1 being expected to run faster than Phase 2, potentially revealing whether a nonce was anticipated.
citation_labels: John Chan et al., Anonymous AE
